task.title: Condition expressions cannot be data-driven: a bound value source is silently inert
task.objective: Owner decision received: Option A, literal-only condition expressions. A condition expression is evaluated from its literal; a valueSource attached to a condition is legacy metadata that is never resolved and must never appear to be active. Pin literal-only routing so a refactor cannot activate inert sources, report an attached-but-ignored source as a non-fatal warning, stop the Flow Designer and the random generator from creating new inert bindings, preserve legacy both-field profiles without field loss, and mutation-test the whole contract.

architecture: src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts condition routing is NOT changed. Option A keeps evaluateBoolean(step.value ?? "", …) as the only condition routing channel, and resolveNext stays synchronous.
No second resolution stack is introduced. src/runner/ValueResolver.ts remains the canonical resolver for the step types that actually use it.
Validation must continue to mirror runtime rather than diverge from it: the ignored-source diagnostic describes what the runner does, and does not change what it does.
The inert-source diagnostic uses the existing FlowValidationSeverity warning model, following the degradedWaitCondition precedent. No new severity concept is invented.
security: No secret value may be resolved into a routing decision. A condition valueSource of kind secret stays unresolved under Option A, as it is under current behavior.
Report artifacts under reports/ are gitignored generated evidence and are never described as live product data.
compatibility: Profiles carrying both a condition literal and a valueSource must keep round-tripping without field loss. The warning is a diagnostic, never a mutation.
Opening or saving a profile must not silently delete an inert condition valueSource. Removal is an explicit user action only.
A legacy both-field profile must stay runnable: the ignored-source diagnostic is non-blocking and must not be misclassified as an execution failure.
Unknown persisted fields are preserved, never dropped.
offline: No dependency, network call or runtime resource is added. Implementation and verification run entirely offline against repository data.

acceptance.description: Current condition routing behavior is proven from source and from executed probes, not from comments or the Bead text.
Condition-node population is measured and separated into product-loaded data, test fixtures, generated ephemeral reports and historical frozen evidence, before and after implementation.
An explicit owner decision selecting literal-only or data-driven condition expressions is recorded before any semantic implementation.

Literal-only routing is pinned by executed cases: literal true, literal false, literal plus contradictory valueSource where the literal still wins, source-only rejected before runtime, missing literal rejected, empty literal rejected.
A condition carrying both a valid literal and a valueSource is no longer silently accepted: it emits a non-fatal warning naming the ignored source, and the flow stays runnable.
New authoring no longer creates inert condition bindings: the Flow Designer condition editor never writes a condition valueSource, and the random generator never attaches one.
A legacy condition carrying literal plus source survives load, save without editing, and reload with no field loss; explicit user removal of the ignored source persists.

The focused verifier is mutation-sensitive: it fails when the diagnostic is removed, when the generator or UI reintroduces condition sources, when runtime is changed to prefer the source, and when source-only becomes accepted.
Repository gates pass at the final committed state and the Program Status sources agree.

evidence.command: read src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts, ExpressionEvaluator.ts, StepExecutor.ts, ValueResolver.ts, src/validation/FlowValidator.ts, StepRequirements.ts
evidence.artifact: FlowExecutor.resolveNext is synchronous and routes a condition via evaluateBoolean(step.value ?? "", getValueWithStepResult); step.valueSource is never referenced. StepExecutor.resolveStepValue gives every OTHER value-taking type the opposite precedence (source wins over literal). ValueResolver.resolve is async and is the single canonical resolver.
